detailedExplanation: Verified against The Tiffin Girls’ School Year 9 Physics Curriculum Outline 2026–27 and aligned to AQA GCSE Physics 8463.
A change in gravitational potential energy near Earth’s surface is ΔEₚ = m g Δh, where m is mass, g is gravitational field strength and Δh is the vertical height change.
When an object falls, energy is transferred from its gravitational potential store to its kinetic store. If resistive forces are negligible, the decrease in GPE equals the increase in kinetic energy.
With air resistance or friction, some energy is dissipated to thermal stores of the object and surroundings, so the kinetic-energy gain is smaller than the GPE decrease.
In combined calculations, use conservation of energy to connect mgh and ½mv², while checking whether the question assumes negligible losses.
